meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если это угроза, она будет дорого вам стоить.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought

examples.trans: Dima, this is not what you thought.

examples.trans: Do not hurry, first we need to discuss everything.

examples.text: Я всё время забываю, что вы просто друзья.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'forget', paired with 'забыть'.

examples.text: Я всё время забываю, что вы просто друзья.
examples.trans: I keep forgetting that you are just friends.

examples.trans: And besides, you are simply a pig.

examples.trans: Alright, let us go there.

examples.trans: Are you free right now, we need to talk.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, я сейчас поеду на работу.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуй').

examples.trans: Do not worry, she will not last long here.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: А вас я попрошу здесь остаться.
examples.trans: And I will ask you to stay here.
There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как же ты меня уже достала!
examples.trans: How sick and tired I am of you already!
I have already understood everything perfectly.
Maxim, you are already a grown boy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'рослый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('grown-up, adult').

examples.trans: Maxim, you are already a grown boy.
He's already grown up.
Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Maxim, you are already a grown boy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('serious').

examples.text: У меня на Викторию Сергеевну планы серьёзные.
examples.trans: I have serious plans for Victoria Sergeyevna.

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lost', paired with 'терять'.

examples.text: А ты уже потерял своё счастье.
examples.trans: And you already lost your happiness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'частье'). Common neuter noun meaning 'happiness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And you already lost your happiness.
